json.postContent:
Your best individual contributor just became your worst manager. 

We’ve all seen it happen: a brilliant engineer or salesperson gets promoted because they are great at their job. But suddenly, the team culture starts to crumble. 

This is the "accidental manager" trap. 

Promoting someone based on technical skill without training them in leadership is a recipe for disaster. Being a high performer is about "me," but being a great manager is about "we." 

If you want to stop accidental managers from sinking your team, keep these three things in mind:

1️⃣ Technical expertise does not equal leadership talent. Recognize the difference between a great doer and a great mentor.

2️⃣ Provide training before the promotion. If you aren’t investing in management skills, you aren’t setting your people up to win.

3️⃣ Focus on emotional intelligence. The best managers are those who prioritize communication, empathy, and team growth over just hitting tasks.

Stop promoting by default. Start building leaders by design. 🚀

https://www.fastcompany.com/91559648/how-accidental-managers-sink-teams-and-sour-workplaces
